newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital car curb plan sparks panic - paper.
newsitem.headline: China capital car curb plan sparks panic - paper.

text.p: Plans by city leaders to limit the number of new cars permitted on the streets of Beijing have aroused concerns among manufacturers and sparked a buying spree by worried consumers, the China Daily said on Thursday.
Authorities in the capital had decided to limit the number of additional motor vehicles to try to ease huge traffic jams clogging its alleys and avenues, the official newspaper said.

"Beijing's plan presents a strong challenge to the country's auto industry and market as well as the government decision-making mechanism," it said in a report that hinted at disagreement between city and national officials on the issue.
"More people are asking if Beijing's decision...is the result of a full investigation and consultation," it said.

Talk of the plan to limit the number of cars on the road has helped boost long-stagnant sales temporarily by triggering a rush to buy cars. But the restrictions, if implemented, would eventually cut into business.

Sales at Beijing's biggest auto market had jumped to 2,000 vehicles so far in March from 1,800 in all of February, but the increase was not reassuring hard-pressed retailers who were concerned by the market's long term prospects, it said.

Officials of the Ministry of Public Security, which is responsible for traffic control and would be required to approve a car curb, believed congestion in Beijing was caused by management problems, not by an excess of vehicles, it said.

Fears that Beijing's intentions on car curbs would develop into action were boosted by the capital's failure to rescind a regulation that bans most economy cars from its streets on alternate days, China Daily said.
The State Council, or cabinet, had in August demanded that all rules discriminating against economy cars be scrapped immediately, but the Beijing ban remained in force, it said.
"Analysts said it is rare for implementation of a State Council document to be delayed so long," it said without elaborating.
